key_insights: Modern fact-checking follows a pipeline: claim detection -> evidence retrieval -> cross-referencing -> confidence scoring
Dual RAG architecture is emerging as best practice: one retriever for trusted/internal sources, one for live external sources, with automatic discrepancy detection
Minimum viable evidence standard: at least 2 independent high-quality sources for any novel claim
Restricting AI analysis to user-uploaded/trusted documents as grounding can cut hallucinations by 60%+
AI fact-checker accuracy reached 72.3% in controlled studies (August 2024) -- useful but not sufficient alone
Source credibility scoring combines: academic signals (peer review, citations), textual signals (bias detection, fallacies), and metadata signals (domain age, corrections policy)
TrustRank and Knowledge-Based Trust (KBT) algorithms use web link structure and fact verification against knowledge bases respectively
Contradiction scanning (searching for 'contradicts', 'retraction', 'fails to replicate' alongside key terms) is a practical technique for finding counter-evidence
Recency window filtering: default to last 24 months for fast-moving topics, expand for historical claims
Mean pooling of statement-level credibility scores produces document-level trust scores

Citation chain verification: follow citation chains to primary sources, verify claims match cited content
Temporal filtering: apply recency windows appropriate to topic velocity (24 months for tech, 5+ years for established science)
Source credibility scoring: combine domain authority, author credentials, publication venue, citation count, and peer review status
Hallucination detection: compare LLM outputs against retrieved source text, flag unsupported claims

Mean pooling of per-claim scores to produce document-level credibility assessments

key_insights: Token inflation from Chain-of-Thought reasoning is a critical bottleneck -- CoT can 3-10x token usage with diminishing returns
Poor data serialization consumes 40-70% of available tokens through unnecessary formatting overhead
Selective token-level optimization outperforms naive breadth -- going deeper on fewer tokens beats going broader
In multi-agent systems, giving each agent full shared context is wasteful -- selective context routing (RCR-Router pattern) is more efficient
4-5 sub-agents per team is the sweet spot for efficiency (confirmed by Team 3's findings in TEAM-0003 session log)
Multi-agent systems frequently underperform single-agent baselines due to coordination overhead (MAST taxonomy: 41.77% design failures, 36.94% coordination failures)
Caching strategies: KV-cache for LLM inference, semantic caching for repeated similar queries, result caching with TTL for API responses
Asynchronous operations with parallel fan-out for independent queries, sequential deepening for dependent queries
Algorithmic progress reducing inference costs ~3x per year independent of hardware improvements
Iterative refinement strategy: start broad to identify promising directions, then go deep on highest-signal areas
techniques: Token-efficient data serialization: use compact formats (CSV, TSV) instead of verbose JSON/XML when passing data to LLMs
Semantic caching: hash query embeddings to detect and serve cached results for semantically similar (not just identical) queries
Result caching with TTL: cache API responses with time-to-live appropriate to data freshness needs (minutes for news, days for academic)
Parallel fan-out: execute independent searches/API calls simultaneously, merge results
Sequential deepening: only drill down on high-signal results, skip low-relevance branches early
Selective context routing: give each agent only the context it needs, not the full shared memory
Prompt compression: remove formatting overhead, use abbreviations, strip boilerplate before sending to LLM
Iterative refinement with early stopping: set quality thresholds and stop searching when met rather than exhausting all sources
Batch API requests where possible: many APIs support bulk queries (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar) that are more efficient than individual calls
Progressive disclosure: gather summaries first, only fetch full content for high-relevance items
improvement_ideas_for_team3: Implement semantic caching: before making API calls, check if a semantically similar query was recently answered

Implement progressive disclosure: fetch abstracts/summaries first, only retrieve full text for items passing relevance threshold

Implement iterative broadening: start with narrow high-precision queries, progressively broaden only if insufficient results found
